title: Multiplication of Whole Numbers by 1- and 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Multiplication – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Multiply whole numbers by 2-digit numbers up to 50 using the grid and vertical methods; revise basic multiplication facts. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on multiplication: multiplying by 1-digit numbers, grid (area) method, long multiplication by 2-digit numbers, 3-digit by 2-digit numbers and estimating products. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply by the units, then by the tens
key_sub: Add the two lines to get the answer.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Know your times tables up to 12 × 12.
  • Grid method: split each number into tens and units, multiply each part and add.
  • Vertical method: multiply by the units digit, then by the tens digit (put a 0 first), then add the two lines.

Examples

Example

34 × 26

34 × 6 = 204

34 × 20 = 680

204 + 680

Answer: 884

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the 0 when multiplying by tens34 × 20 = 680, not 68.
Forgetting to add the carried numberWrite carried numbers small above the next digit.
Adding instead of multiplyingTimes means groups of.

items.q: The ones gave 48: write 8, regroup 4. Now the tens: 5 × 6. What do you do?
items.e: Multiply first, then add the regrouped 4: 5 × 6 + 4 = 34. Write 4 in the tens place and regroup 3 hundreds. Full answer: Ones: 8 × 6 = 48. Write 8, regroup 4 tens. Tens: 5 × 6 + 4 = 34. Write 4, regroup 3 hundreds. Hundreds: 8 × 6 + 3 = 51. Write 51. Answer: 5,148.

items.q: Round 3,746 to the nearest thousand to estimate 3,746 × 4.
items.e: 3,746 has 7 hundreds, so it rounds up to 4,000. 4,000 × 4 = 16,000. The exact answer is 14,984.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest ten to estimate 67 × 48.
items.e: 67 rounds up to 70 and 48 rounds up to 50. 70 × 50 = 3,500. The exact answer is 3,216, close to the estimate.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest ten to estimate 83 × 26.

items.q: Round 624 to the nearest hundred and 58 to the nearest ten to estimate 624 × 58.

items.q: The school tuck shop sells 312 plates of fried rice each week. About how many plates does it sell in 8 weeks?
items.e: Round 312 to the nearest hundred: 300. 300 × 8 = 2,400. Do not round 8 to 10: that gives 3,000, which is too far off. The exact answer is 312 × 8 = 2,496.

items.q: A theatre sells 1,985 tickets for each show. About how many tickets does it sell for 4 shows?
items.e: Round 1,985 to the nearest thousand: 2,000. 2,000 × 4 = 8,000. (Rounding 1,985 down to 1,000 gives 4,000, far too small.) The exact answer is 1,985 × 4 = 7,940.

items.q: A stadium has 48 rows with 215 seats in each row. About how many seats are there?
items.e: Round 215 to 200 and 48 to 50. 200 × 50 = 10,000. (Rounding 48 down to 40 gives 8,000.) The exact answer is 215 × 48 = 10,320.

items.q: Funke reads 28 pages of a storybook each day. About how many pages does she read in 31 days?
items.e: Round 28 to 30 and 31 to 30. 30 × 30 = 900. (Using 20 × 30 = 600 rounds 28 the wrong way.) The exact answer is 28 × 31 = 868.
